post.description:
Ask Paddle to refund an **unused** pack in full. The lot is frozen and a durable intent written
first; a pack with spent or running units goes to manual review instead. The units are taken back only
when Paddle reports the refund approved. Repeating the call never creates a second refund.

Add or remove credits. Repeating the same `idempotency_key` changes nothing and reports `applied:
false`.

post.description: Always 204: the response never reveals whether the address has an account.

One generic failure for every cause (wrong password, unknown address, an account with no password), and
a real hash check even for an unknown address, so neither the body nor the response time says which. A
throttle is not a lockout: past the limit the answer is 429, and the right password works again once the
window has passed.
Needs the current password. Signs out every session including this one: the person logs in again.

Always 202. A reset link is mailed only when the address has an account, and nothing in the answer says
whether it does. The link goes to the configured app origin, never to a host taken from the request.

Set the password (the first one, for an account made by Google or a magic link) and sign everyone out.
Nobody is signed in by this: the person logs in again with the new password.

Re-mail a pending registration with a fresh token (the old link stops working). The password hash
stays the one chosen at registration; an address with no pending registration gets nothing.

The seller's document for this sale, obtained from Paddle on demand after the ownership check.
Paddle is the seller and issues it; the product issues no second customer invoice for the same sale.

delete.description:
Erase the account. Idempotent and retryable: the processor is erased first, so a failure at either
step leaves
the request safe to repeat (deleting an already deleted Stripe customer succeeds).

get.description: Profile, plan, credits, feature flags and the Otodom circuit-breaker state, in one call for the SPA.
Everything we hold about the caller as one JSON document (access request). Limited to 5 per hour.
Newest first. `limit` may reach the per-account cap, so `limit=500` returns every saved listing.
